focus: Spec-track narrowing proof, power, and hardening
noveltyJustification: All four findings extend pre-existing track-narrowing results with direct checks of current scoring code, repeat summary, and tests; each is partially new to this lineage, none wholly new.

label: P0 — Keep hard spec-track narrowing offline: the 017 keep (97/256 vs 68/256) and 049 margin stop (106/270 vs 82/270, CI [-0.1185, 0.2760]) are inconclusive evidence, not a live win or clean kill; settle with a powered time-held-out real Gate 1 test.

P0 — Pre-register an independent real-request holdout, labels, alpha, MDE, power, absolute accuracy and per-track recall floors against the strongest safe baseline; the observed 0.588 decided-pair rate needs about 217 decided pairs (~431 rows) for 80% power, while the 270-row repeat had 0.399 power.

P1 — Do not tune on capped packet-description rows or adopt probability-aware/one-call arms from proxy gains: the live test set caps rows at 20 per track, the paraphrase probe favored ripgrep 8–2, and the repeat scored probability-aware A=102 vs modal A=106 and one-call A=103; diagnose per-track confusion before changing question/options.

P1 — Retain row/model pins, replay, no-overwrite and cluster-bootstrap coverage as reproducibility safeguards, but require external labels and real holdout data before gated shadow integration; confirm by replaying the pinned report and checking featureReady-off/missing-auth preserve broad-search behavior.
